stem: Fresh transplants occupy only a small portion of a much larger container, and large irrigation events keep the unrooted lower media wet for long periods. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: Increase fertilizer strength because a small root system needs a more concentrated solution while it expands into the larger container, then keep the mature irrigation schedule unchanged
Keep the full container saturated so new roots encounter uniformly wet media as they grow toward the bottom and outer edges
Match irrigation to current root occupancy, media behavior, and measured depletion rather than applying a mature-container schedule immediately
Base irrigation mainly on canopy height because plant size is a more direct measure of water demand than root-zone moisture patterns
rationale: Young root systems may not use water throughout the full container volume. Irrigation should reflect current root occupancy and measured root-zone behavior rather than assuming mature demand immediately after transplant.
